## Purpose and build shape
Official Kotlin/Android client for connecting devices to Home Assistant servers, exposing the server UI plus native Android capabilities (sensors, notifications, controls, widgets, Assist, NFC, vehicle, and Wear OS). Gradle builds three principal apps: handset (`app`), Wear OS (`wear`), and Android Automotive (`automotive`), with shared domain/data infrastructure in `common`. Variant source sets distinguish `full` and `minimal` handset capabilities.
- `settings.gradle.kts`
- `app/build.gradle.kts`
- `common/build.gradle.kts`

## Process entry points and composition
Android manifests register the application components; application classes initialize dependency injection and platform behavior. Handset startup enters `LaunchActivity`, which selects onboarding or the connected frontend. Additional OS-owned entry points include notification, Quick Settings, voice-assistant, controls, widget, and automotive services.
- `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`
- `app/src/main/kotlin/io/homeassistant/companion/android/HomeAssistantApplication.kt`
- `app/src/main/kotlin/io/homeassistant/companion/android/launch/LaunchActivity.kt`

## Server, authentication, and persistence boundary
`common` owns server selection, authenticated HTTP integration calls, TLS/trust handling, WebSocket protocol types, preferences, and Room persistence. Repository interfaces separate consumers from Retrofit/HTTP, socket, Android keystore, and database implementations. The Room database persists server/session metadata, sensor configuration, notifications, tiles, and widget state.
- `common/src/main/kotlin/io/homeassistant/companion/android/common/data/servers/ServerManager.kt`
- `common/src/main/kotlin/io/homeassistant/companion/android/common/data/authentication/AuthenticationRepository.kt`
- `common/src/main/kotlin/io/homeassistant/companion/android/database/AppDatabase.kt`

## Primary Home Assistant data flow
After registration/authentication, feature layers use integration repositories for REST-style device registration, sensor updates, actions, and location updates; long-lived WebSocket repositories carry entity state, registry, template, conversation/Assist, Matter, and Thread responses/events. App-level `WebsocketManager` manages handset connectivity and reacts to Android lifecycle/network events.
- `common/src/main/kotlin/io/homeassistant/companion/android/common/data/integration/IntegrationRepository.kt`
- `common/src/main/kotlin/io/homeassistant/companion/android/common/data/websocket/WebSocketRepository.kt`
- `app/src/main/kotlin/io/homeassistant/companion/android/websocket/WebsocketManager.kt`

## Handset experience: frontend and onboarding
The default experience is a native Compose shell around the Home Assistant web frontend. `FrontendViewModel` drives URL/session/UI state; handlers bridge WebView or JavaScript requests to native capabilities such as permissions, downloads, barcode scanning, dialogs, haptics, media, Bluetooth Improv provisioning, and Matter/Thread. First-run and server-change flows are a native Compose onboarding graph for discovery, manual server setup, connectivity/security, device naming, and location choices.
- `app/src/main/kotlin/io/homeassistant/companion/android/frontend/FrontendScreen.kt`
- `app/src/main/kotlin/io/homeassistant/companion/android/frontend/handler/FrontendMessageHandler.kt`
- `app/src/main/kotlin/io/homeassistant/companion/android/onboarding/serverdiscovery/HomeAssistantSearcher.kt`

## Native capability pipelines
Sensor managers collect Android and device state; receivers/workers schedule updates, while `SensorRepository` serializes registration and uploads to Home Assistant. Native surfaces consume the same server/integration layer: Android Controls map HA entities to system controls; widgets store configuration locally and invoke HA actions; FCM receives server push notifications and routes actions. Assist combines voice-interaction services, audio strategies, Home Assistant assist pipelines, TTS, and optional bundled TensorFlow Lite wake-word models via a JNI/C++ module.
- `common/src/main/kotlin/io/homeassistant/companion/android/common/sensors/SensorUpdater.kt`
- `app/src/main/kotlin/io/homeassistant/companion/android/controls/HaControlsProviderService.kt`
- `app/src/main/kotlin/io/homeassistant/companion/android/assist/service/AssistVoiceInteractionService.kt`

## Wear, automotive, and external infrastructure
Wear is a distinct Wear OS app with onboarding, home/entity views, complications, tiles, health sensors, phone data exchange, and FCM; it shares `common` persistence/protocol abstractions. Automotive contributes its own manifest while handset code contains the car-app service/screens. Full variants integrate Google Play services for Matter/Thread and Firebase Cloud Messaging; native wake-word execution uses CMake/JNI. CI runs GitHub Actions, including emulator E2E against a checked-in Home Assistant fixture.
- `wear/src/main/kotlin/io/homeassistant/companion/android/splash/SplashActivity.kt`
- `app/src/full/kotlin/io/homeassistant/companion/android/matter/MatterManagerImpl.kt`
- `microwakeword/src/main/cpp/MicroWakeWord_jni.cpp`
